title: Navigating Financial Success: Retirement Savings While Raising a Child with Developmental Disabilities
summary: Learn strategies for balancing retirement savings while raising a child with developmental disabilities, from special-needs trusts to long-term planning.
body_text: Navigating Financial Success: Retirement Savings While Raising a Child with Developmental Disabilities Published on July 22, 2026 | 3 min read | Webster Bank Being a high earner not rich yet (HENRY) may come with financial challenges. When coupled with the responsibility of raising a child with developmental disabilities, you might need thoughtful financial planning even more. Here are a few strategies that may help you save for retirement while managing your child’s well-being. Craft a Comprehensive Financial Plan A comprehensive financial plan should take into account both your short-term and long-term goals. Begin by assessing your current financial situation, including income, expenses, and debt. Then, factor in the additional costs associated with raising a child with developmental disabilities, such as therapy, specialized education, and medical expenses. Creating a detailed financial roadmap provides clarity and can help you allocate your resources. Consider consulting with a financial professional who specializes in working with families facing special needs. They may provide personalized insights for your specific circumstances. Establish a Special-Needs Trust One essential element of financial planning for families with children with developmental disabilities is establishing a special-needs trust (SNT). An SNT is a legal instrument designed to provide financial support for a person with a disability without jeopardizing their eligibility for government benefits like Medicaid and Supplemental Security Income. Through an SNT, you may contribute funds for your child’s future care and well-being while safeguarding their access to essential government assistance programs. Work with an attorney experienced in special needs planning so the trust meets your child’s specific requirements. Retirement Contributions As a HENRY, take advantage of retirement savings opportunities to build a robust financial foundation. Contribute to your employer-sponsored retirement plan, like a 401(k) or 457, and capture any available employer match. Additionally, consider contributing to an individual retirement account (IRA) or Roth IRA to diversify your retirement savings further. While balancing the financial demands of raising a child with developmental disabilities, consistently contributing to retirement accounts helps build a nest egg for your future. Automate your contributions to make saving a seamless part of your financial routine. Explore Government Assistance Programs Research government assistance programs that may provide financial support for families with children with developmental disabilities. You may be eligible for state or federal programs that offer financial aid, respite care, or other types of assistance. Plan for the Unexpected Review and update your insurance policies to determine if your family has adequate insurance coverage for unexpected events. Life insurance, disability insurance, and long-term care insurance are crucial components of a comprehensive risk management strategy. Insurance coverage may help your family in the event of unforeseen circumstances. Work with an insurance professional to assess your coverage and make necessary adjustments based on your evolving needs. Look for Community and Support Networks Building a community of support is invaluable for HENRYs navigating the complexities of raising a child with developmental disabilities. Connect with other parents facing similar challenges, join support groups, and seek out resources within your community. Shared experiences may offer practical insights and emotional support, helping you navigate the joys and challenges of parenting a child with special needs. Important Disclosures The opinions voiced in this material are for general information only and are not intended to provide specific advice or recommendations for any individual. To determine which investment(s) or insurance product(s) may be appropriate for you, consult your financial professional prior to investing or purchasing. This information is not intended to be a substitute for individualized legal advice. Please consult your legal advisor regarding your specific situation. This article was prepared by WriterAccess. title: What Makes a Leadership Legacy Last? Reflections on Clemens Scholz’s 26-Year Career at Novanta
summary: By Johannes Tschepe, Senior VP Global Sales & Marketing When people talk about successful leaders, they often focus on business results or growth milestones. body_text: By Johannes Tschepe, Senior VP Global Sales & Marketing When people talk about successful leaders, they often focus on business results or growth milestones. Those achievements matter, but the most enduring leaders leave behind something greater. As Vice President, Marketing Clemens Scholz retires after 26 years in medical technology, I have been reflecting on what made his career so impactful. His accomplishments were significant. He helped grow a leading Advanced Surgery business and championed lean operating principles, advancing technologies that strengthened our market position and supporting strategic growth initiatives across the organization. His influence extended beyond operational and product innovation into long-term business strategy, where he helped identify and evaluate opportunities that continue to shape our future direction. What distinguished Clemens, however, was not only what he accomplished, but how he accomplished it. Clemens studied mechanical engineering and medicine and wrote his Ph.D. thesis in Biomedical Engineering. He brought a rare ability to connect technical, clinical and business perspectives. He could quickly understand complex challenges and identify meaningful opportunities, helping teams find practical solutions. That combination of knowledge and curiosity made him particularly effective in identifying emerging opportunities and seeing potential where others might not yet see it. Equally important was his commitment to integrity. Throughout his career, Clemens consistently chose the path that aligned with his principles, even when it was not the easiest option. That authenticity earned the trust and respect of employees throughout the organization. Employees always knew where they stood with Clemens. He was honest and approachable, creating an environment where people felt empowered to contribute and innovate. As the organization grew, he remained deeply connected to everyone and genuinely interested in their success. Innovation was equally central to his leadership style. Clemens encouraged employees to challenge assumptions and explore new ideas, always thinking beyond conventional solutions. His curiosity and willingness to invest in people helped create a culture where innovation could thrive. What stands out most is the balance he maintained between driving results and supporting people. While leading substantial business growth and technological advancement, he never lost sight of the individuals behind those achievements. Employees remember a leader who knew them personally and encouraged them, consistently bringing positive energy to the workplace. Clemens’ influence also extended beyond business performance. Through volunteer efforts and charitable initiatives, he demonstrated that leadership is ultimately about serving others and making a meaningful difference. As our industry continues to evolve, the lessons from Clemens’ career remain as relevant as ever: Prepare thoroughly. Stay curious. Support innovation. Respect diverse perspectives. Lead with integrity. Never lose sight of people. These principles shaped Clemens Scholz’s extraordinary 26-year career and will continue to influence the teams and leaders that follow. That is what makes a legacy last.

title: DigitalOwl vs Wisedocs vs Codes Health
summary: Compare Codes Health, DigitalOwl, and Wisedocs for personal injury and mass tort medical record retrieval and AI analysis. See how each platform handles retrieval, turnaround, pricing structure, and plaintiff-side case workflows.
body_text: Personal injury and mass tort law firms face a critical bottleneck: medical records that take months to retrieve and hours of manual review once they arrive. DigitalOwl, Wisedocs, and Codes Health all use AI to speed up parts of this process, but their approaches differ. Codes Health is built specifically for plaintiff-side retrieval and case development, combining medical record retrieval with AI-powered organization and analysis in one workflow. This comparison breaks down what each platform delivers and which solution best fits plaintiff-focused legal workflows. Codes Health is built around eliminating the fragmentation that comes from managing retrieval and analysis as two separate vendor relationships, delivering AI-organized records in a couple of weeks rather than months. Key Takeaways Codes Health combines medical record retrieval and AI-powered analysis in a single plaintiff-focused workflow, so firms are not managing two separate vendor relationships for these functions Codes Health delivers complete records in a couple of weeks, not months, and does not offer same-day retrieval Competitors offering same-day retrieval typically deliver incomplete records that require ongoing client involvement to resolve gaps, which can lead to churn. Codes Health retrieves complete records in a couple of weeks, not months DigitalOwl, now part of Datavant, is expanding into combined retrieval and analysis through its Datavant and Ontellus integration and a rebrand to ChartSwap Insights, a recent shift from its longtime analysis-only model Wisedocs is built primarily for insurance carriers, TPAs, and defense-side legal teams, with SOC 2 Type II certification and AI models trained on over 100 million documents Filevine users can access Codes Health directly inside the case file, submitting requests, tracking status, and receiving organized records without leaving the platform Understanding the Core: Medical Record Review Services in Litigation and Claims Medical record review has become the foundation of personal injury case development. The process involves retrieving records from multiple providers, organizing thousands of pages chronologically, extracting diagnoses and treatment patterns, and identifying case-critical facts that support damages calculations and causation arguments. For plaintiff firms, this workflow creates significant operational challenges: Traditional retrieval can take weeks to months through manual fax, phone, and mail processes Large medical record sets can require many hours of attorney or paralegal review time when handled manually Fragmented vendor relationships (one service for retrieval, another for analysis, plus internal staff for organization) add coordination overhead Incomplete records discovered late can derail settlement negotiations or trial preparation The AI clinical documentation market was valued at roughly $1.23 billion in 2023 and is projected to grow substantially over the next decade, reflecting significant investment in solving these problems. Not all solutions address the full workflow, though. Many focus exclusively on analysis, leaving retrieval to traditional vendors or internal staff. The distinction that matters : platforms that only analyze records still depend on someone else to retrieve them first. Codes Health's approach is built around closing that gap by handling retrieval and analysis together. Codes Health: AI-Powered Retrieval and Analysis Platform for Law Firms Codes Health operates as a technology platform combining retrieval operations, AI powered analysis, and human verification in a single solution built specifically for plaintiff law firms. What Makes Codes Health Different Integrated retrieval and analysis : Codes Health handles the workflow from request submission through organized delivery. The platform connects with claims clearinghouses, custodian integrations, proprietary provider networks, fax, and patient portals. Plaintiff-specific design : The platform targets seven legal practice areas: personal injury, mass torts, medical malpractice, workers' compensation, disability law, insurance litigation, and wrongful death. Features such as demand letter support and billing analysis are built around plaintiff-side case development. AI-human hybrid verification : Codes Health combines automated AI processing with human verification. Medical, legal, or operational specialists validate findings and confirm retrieved materials match the original request. Proactive error prevention : Incomplete authorizations are a leading cause of denied requests. Missing patient signatures, unclear expiration dates, or unchecked boxes for sensitive records can restart the federal 30-day authorization clock (state rules vary). The platform's AI reviews every request before submission, flagging misspellings, missing dates of service, and signature issues that would otherwise cause provider rejections. Flat-fee pricing : Codes Health uses flat-fee pricing rather than per-page charges, providing cost predictability that aligns with contingency-fee economics. Continuous platform evolution : Codes Health's engineering team, including MIT-educated engineers, continuously builds out additional workflows and products, helping the platform evolve to meet the changing demands of modern legal practices. The Filevine Partnership: Embedded Workflow for Legal Teams In July 2026, Filevine announced a strategic partnership that embeds Codes Health's medical record retrieval directly into the Filevine legal case management environment. The integration goes beyond a standard third-party connection. What Filevine users can do : Submit medical record requests directly from the relevant case file Track request status in real time without leaving Filevine Communicate with the Codes Health team from within the case workflow Receive completed medical records, billing records, and imaging inside the Filevine project Codes Health validates authorizations, date ranges, and provider-specific requirements before submission, manages provider follow-up across calls, faxes, emails, and portals, and verifies completeness before records are returned. For firms using Filevine as their case management system, this reduces the context switching between platforms that traditionally fragments retrieval workflows. Speed and Accuracy: The Differentiators in Medical Record Retrieval Speed in medical records means little without completeness. A platform that delivers partial records quickly but requires weeks of follow-up to obtain the full set has not actually saved time. Comparing Turnaround Times Codes Health delivers complete, organized records in a couple of weeks rather than the months typical of traditional retrieval, maintaining daily provider follow-ups so requests do not stall in provider queues. DigitalOwl , now operating under Datavant, processes uploaded records quickly (the company states results in under an hour for review and analysis). Its retrieval capability is newer and is being built out through Datavant's 2025 acquisitions of DigitalOwl and Ontellus, along with a rebrand toward "ChartSwap Insights" positioned as combining retrieval and analysis. Firms evaluating DigitalOwl today should confirm directly with the company how much of the retrieval workflow is production-ready versus still rolling out. Wisedocs provides fast AI analysis for records already retrieved, generally within hours for a processed file. The platform's core focus remains analysis for insurance carriers and defense-side legal teams rather than plaintiff-side retrieval. The same-day retrieval question : some vendors in this space advertise same-day or rapid retrieval. These services can deliver incomplete records that require ongoing client involvement to resolve gaps, which creates churn and can extend total turnaround time. Codes Health does not offer same-day retrieval. It retrieves complete records in a couple of weeks, not months, aiming to reduce the back-and-forth that fragments workflows. Cost Structure Differences Total cost of ownership depends heavily on firm volume, contract terms, and whether retrieval and analysis are purchased separately or as one service. Analysis-only platforms like DigitalOwl's legacy self-serve tools and Wisedocs typically require a separate retrieval relationship (vendor or in-house staff), which adds coordination overhead even when software licensing itself is inexpensive. Codes Health's flat-fee model combines both functions under one relationship, which can simplify budgeting for contingency-fee firms. Specific competitor pricing is not published on their websites, so firms should request current quotes directly from each vendor before comparing costs. Ensuring Data Integrity with Hybrid Verification All three platforms employ AI, but their verification approaches differ: Codes Health : AI-human hybrid verification, with specialists confirming findings match original requests DigitalOwl : AI-driven summarization and de-duplication, with the company reporting up to 90 percent reduction in page counts and a click-to-evidence feature linking insights back to source documents Wisedocs : AI processing with human clinician review and source-linked citations in chronologies For litigation, the key question is whether outputs are defensible at deposition and trial. Source-linked citations and human verification both support this, but verification matters less if records are incomplete to begin with. Bridging the Gap: Integrated Solutions for Claims Management and Legal Review The fragmentation problem in medical records goes beyond retrieval timelines. When firms use separate systems for case management, record retrieval, and AI analysis, information scatters across platforms. The Power of Native Integrations Codes Health's Filevine partnership demonstrates what embedded workflow integration looks like in practice. Rather than exporting data to a retrieval vendor and then importing analyzed records back into case files, everything stays connected to the relevant matter. Benefits for legal teams : A single operational record per case, rather than scattered files across vendor portals Real-time visibility into retrieval progress without vendor check-ins Reduced administrative burden from managing multiple relationships Completed records delivered directly into case files ready for review For high-volume practices managing many active cases, this consolidation can translate into meaningful time savings and fewer requests falling through the cracks. Custom Integrations for High-Volume Firms Beyond the Filevine partnership, Codes Health can build custom integrations with CRM platforms and other legal or medical software for high-volume customers, allowing firms to maintain existing workflows while adding retrieval and AI analysis capabilities. AI-Powered Insights: Transforming Medical Records into Actionable Intelligence Raw medical records require significant interpretation before they support case development. AI analysis promises to accelerate this process, but platform capabilities vary. Extracting Key Information Beyond Basic Summarization General AI platforms like ChatGPT are not designed for litigation-grade medical record review and are not reliable for this kind of analysis. Codes Health's AI platform is purpose-built for medical record analysis in a legal context. Codes Health's insights extraction identifies: Diagnoses and treatment patterns across providers Potential breaches in care Documented future medical needs and expenses Missed appointments and treatment gaps Pre-existing conditions requiring case strategy consideration The platform also offers an intake copilot-style interface that lets users ask questions about a patient's history rather than manually searching every document. DigitalOwl focuses on medical chronology generation with de-duplication, reporting 97 percent accuracy and up to 72 percent time savings on its own site, helping users navigate large record sets. The platform was built primarily for insurance underwriting and P&C claims before expanding into legal use cases. Wisedocs provides page-level citations in chronologies with automated extraction of treatment information. The platform states its AI models are trained on more than 100 million documents. Missing Record Detection: A Notable Capability Codes Health's missing records review compares delivered records against original requests and patient treatment history, identifying gaps before attorneys open the file. This proactive flagging is designed to help prevent discovering incomplete records during depositions or trial preparation. Why this matters : treatment notes from a specialist referenced in primary care records but never received could contain the causation opinion that makes or breaks a case. Systematic completeness verification catches these gaps when they can still be addressed. The Competitive Landscape: DigitalOwl, Wisedocs, and Codes Health's Positioning Each platform occupies a distinct market position based on heritage, target customers, and core capabilities. DigitalOwl: Insurance Heritage Now Under Datavant DigitalOwl was originally built for insurance underwriting and P&C carriers, with personal injury and mass tort use cases added as the platform expanded. In late 2025, Datavant completed its acquisition of DigitalOwl and separately acquired retrieval provider Ontellus, and the company has since signaled a rebrand toward "ChartSwap Insights" aimed at bringing retrieval and analysis together. Key characteristics as described on its own site: Fast AI processing: under one hour turnaround for chronology generation on uploaded records Reported 97 percent accuracy and up to 72 percent reduction in review time De-duplication reducing page counts by up to 90 percent HIPAA and SOC 2 compliant The platform's insurance heritage means many of its workflows were originally designed for claims triage. Its retrieval capabilities are newer and are still being integrated following the Datavant and Ontellus acquisitions, so firms should confirm current retrieval functionality directly with DigitalOwl. Wisedocs: Defense and Carrier Focus Wisedocs targets insurance carriers, TPAs, and defense-side legal practices. Key characteristics as described on its own site: SOC 2 Type II and HIPAA compliant Human-reviewed chronologies with source-linked citations AI models trained on more than 100 million documents Primarily a defense and claims-side tool rather than a plaintiff retrieval platform Wisedocs does not publish pricing on its website, so cost comparisons require a direct quote. Its defense and carrier focus means its workflows are generally built around claims triage and panel firm coordination rather than plaintiff demand package development. Codes Health: Plaintiff-First with Integrated Retrieval Codes Health was purpose-built for plaintiff practices from day one. Key characteristics: Combines retrieval and AI analysis in one plaintiff-focused workflow Plaintiff-specific workflows for personal injury, mass tort, and medical malpractice Flat-fee pricing aligned with contingency-fee economics Proactive error prevention that flags authorization issues before submission Missing record detection built into the completeness review process For plaintiff firms choosing between these platforms, the question isn't just which AI processes faster, but which solution addresses the full workflow from request through organized delivery. Compliance and Security in Medical Record Handling All three platforms handle protected health information, making HIPAA compliance mandatory. Platform Compliance Codes Health : HIPAA compliant platform with business associate agreements available for customers DigitalOwl : HIPAA and SOC 2 compliant, per its own site Wisedocs : HIPAA compliant and SOC 2 Type II certified, per its own site For plaintiff firms, the practical compliance question is whether outputs support trial admissibility. All three platforms provide audit trails and source documentation, but completeness verification at the retrieval stage supports stronger chain-of-custody documentation for the firms that rely on it. Growth and Strategic Partnerships: A Look at Market Traction Market validation comes from customer adoption and strategic partnerships. Codes Health's Position Founded : 2024, by graduates of MIT and Yale Customer base : trusted by hundreds of firms across personal injury, mass tort, and medical malpractice Investors : Y Combinator, Amplify Partners, Haystack, General Catalyst, Night Capital, and Pathlight Ventures Strategic partnership : Filevine embedded integration, announced July 2026 The Filevine partnership represents significant validation. Filevine CEO Ryan Anderson described medical record retrieval as a long-standing customer pain point, positioning Codes Health as the solution built into Filevine's case management system. Competitor Positioning DigitalOwl was acquired by Datavant in a deal completed in October 2025, alongside Datavant's separate acquisition of retrieval provider Ontellus. This gives DigitalOwl access to retrieval infrastructure it did not previously operate directly, though the combined retrieval and analysis offering is still in the process of rolling out under the ChartSwap Insights rebrand. Wisedocs has built infrastructure processing high volumes for carrier clients. The platform's strength remains defense and claims operations rather than plaintiff litigation. The Bottom Line: Which Platform Fits Your Practice? Choose Codes Health When You Need: A combined solution for retrieval and AI analysis in one plaintiff-focused workflow Plaintiff-specific workflows for PI, mass tort, or medical malpractice Flat-fee pricing aligned with contingency economics Proactive error prevention on record requests Missing record detection before trial Filevine integration with an embedded case file workflow Consider DigitalOwl When You Need: Fast AI processing for records already obtained Insurance-grade analytics for claims evaluation A platform now backed by Datavant's broader retrieval infrastructure Consider Wisedocs When You Need: Defense-side workflows for carrier or TPA clients Infrastructure built for high-volume processing Mixed plaintiff and defense practice flexibility For plaintiff-focused practices, Codes Health offers a workflow purpose-built for litigation, combining retrieval and AI analysis for firms that want to reduce vendor fragmentation. Frequently Asked Questions What are the main problems Codes Health solves for plaintiff law firms? Codes Health addresses three core bottlenecks: retrieval delays (delivering records in a couple of weeks instead of months), workflow fragmentation (combining retrieval and analysis in one relationship), and manual review burden (AI-powered organization and analysis). The platform also flags authorization errors before submission, helping prevent rejected requests that restart provider timelines. How does Codes Health ensure speed and accuracy of medical record retrieval? Codes Health maintains daily provider follow-ups across calls, faxes, emails, and portals. The platform's AI validates authorizations, date ranges, and provider-specific requirements before submission. Human specialists verify that retrieved materials match original requests, and the system compares delivered records against patient history to identify gaps before closing requests. What is the significance of Codes Health's partnership with Filevine? The Filevine partnership, announced in July 2026, embeds Codes Health directly into Filevine's case management environment. Users can submit requests, track status, communicate with Codes Health, and receive completed records without leaving the Filevine project, reducing the context switching that separate vendor portals typically create. How does AI contribute to Codes Health's medical record analysis? Codes Health's AI extracts structured information including diagnoses, treatments, providers, dates, and expenses from unstructured medical records. The platform flags potential breaches in care, identifies documented future medical needs, and surfaces facts like missed appointments and pre-existing conditions. An intake copilot interface lets users ask questions about patient history rather than manually searching documents. What competitive advantage does Codes Health offer compared to DigitalOwl and Wisedocs? Codes Health combines retrieval and AI analysis in a single plaintiff-focused workflow. DigitalOwl is still building out its retrieval capability following its 2025 acquisition by Datavant, and Wisedocs remains centered on defense and carrier-side analysis. Codes Health was built specifically for plaintiff practices from the outset, while DigitalOwl's heritage is insurance underwriting and Wisedocs focuses on defense and carrier clients.
